milestone: Human editor save and load workflow
implemented: First-class editor Save/Load tool using shared native save.* operations; no separate serialization implementation.
Explicit folder/slot observations preserve stale runtime, gameplay, content and slot guards.
Retained failed-operation IDs/parameters; explicit retry or dismissal, root and close-draft protection.
Stopped restore uses an observed trusted C# launch profile or explicit no-gameplay selection; active restore inherits loaded code.
Explicit prior-generation recovery and acknowledged writes preserve corrupt data.
Cheap native save configuration status in desktop polling makes external configuration changes visible without disk reads.
Compact human controls with conditional recovery/retry sections and technical details behind an expander.

checks: Actual Save-window controls preserve dirty and stale observations.
Exact pending mutation retry survives explicit observation refresh.
Saved typed C# state and mid-motion door restore in the same and fresh editor processes.
Implicit recovery is refused; explicit load and acknowledged write preserve quarantined payload.
Authored world bytes remain unchanged throughout all phases.
Dirty folder draft prevents both tool-window and main-editor close, with a persistent explanation.

review_fixes: Completed native operations remain successful if presentation refresh fails; the result stays available.
A delayed folder-picker result cannot overwrite a newer folder draft or configuration observation.
Cancelled tool-window close reports its draft/pending guard through persistent model error state.
Initial readable but diagnostic-heavy layout was replaced with a compact main workflow and collapsed details.
limitations: Semantic routed control/HWND tests and attached Avalonia visual-content renders; no physical input, IME or general accessibility qualification.
Windows was locked; no OS window screenshot or desktop compositor qualification.
Native folder-picker interaction and arbitrary DPI/multi-display layouts were not exercised by automation.
Synchronous paused save/load; no autosave scheduler, slot browser, thumbnails or persistent storage-root preferences.
Fixed supported entity set, external verified assets and exact module/backend/schema binding; no general save migration.
Typed gameplay callback Save/Load requests and safe continuous-player handoff remain separate implementation work.
The existing snapshot/storage limits, including physics reconstruction and unqualified power-loss behavior, still apply.
